open_points.subject: Network surface / Cabinet Kernel, PresuPro, Cabinet
open_points.text: the service API for services, reachable only on the production host and over the protected channel (R0-28)
open_points.question: Where do Cabinet Kernel, PresuPro and Cabinet run, and over which channel does each reach the production service API? Only Client Portal's WireGuard path is named, and no agent may run on the production host.
options: all three run on the home server
Kernel and the others run elsewhere and use the WireGuard tunnel or a second named channel
each service gets its own named channel
open_points.default_guess: Services not on the home server reach it over the same home-initiated WireGuard tunnel, each with its own token.

open_points.subject: Personal data vs context answer
open_points.text: The customer's contact data reaches the owner alone.
open_points.question: Does the `customer` field of `context`, sent to PresuPro and Client Portal, carry only the `customer_ref`, or contact data such as the name? If it carries contact data, this sentence contradicts R0-43.
options: context carries customer_ref only
context carries the customer's name, so this sentence is narrowed
Portal gets contact data for client-facing display
open_points.default_guess: context.customer is the customer_ref only; contact data never leaves to a service.

open_points.subject: Consumer services / Cabinet Web mirror
open_points.text: PresuPro, Client Portal, Cabinet, the Cabinet Web mirror. Each authenticates with its own service token
open_points.question: Is the Cabinet Web mirror a consumer with a token, or does it lose access unless it receives one (R0-27)?
options: it receives a token
it is dropped until it does
open_points.default_guess: It is listed as a consumer only once it holds a token; without one it is refused.

open_points.subject: read the latest artifact of a type
open_points.text: | read the latest artifact of a type | owner; a service |
open_points.question: Can Kernel acting for the agent read the latest artifact of any project, or only on its session's project, as R0-41 requires?
options: Kernel only on its session's project
any service on any project
open_points.default_guess: Kernel for the agent only on its session's project; other services as their token allows.

open_points.subject: publish / withdraw an artifact pointer
open_points.text: | publish an artifact pointer | producer service; the owner for any owner service |
open_points.question: The table does not confine Kernel's publish and withdraw to the session's project, but R0-41 does. Which text governs, and what failure does a publish on another project produce?
options: add the confinement and a 'another project than the session's refused' failure
Kernel publishes on any project as a producer
open_points.default_guess: Confined to the session's project, with the same refusal as 'add a room'.

open_points.subject: read a project for a service without personal_data
open_points.text: read a project | owner; a trusted service, in its disclosure class (R0-26)
open_points.question: The card includes the object's address, which is personal_data. What does a service whose token does not allow personal_data receive, given that R0-26 forbids mixed answers?
options: refused
a separate card projection without the object's personal fields
open_points.default_guess: A dedicated non-personal projection of the card; the full card only with the personal_data class.

open_points.subject: restrict processing of a customer
open_points.text: its contact data stays stored but leaves Registry to no one but the owner (R0-37)
open_points.question: Contact data already reaches the owner alone. What observable behaviour does restriction change: list visibility, use in new or existing projects, appearance in context, or the retention clock?
options: blocks naming by new projects and marks the customer in lists
hides the customer_ref from service answers
only a flag shown to the owner
open_points.default_guess: Marks the customer in owner views, and a new project may not name it.

open_points.subject: agent sessions
open_points.text: choose the working project | owner, for one agent session ... unknown session refused
open_points.question: How does Registry come to know a session so the owner can pick it and Registry can refuse an unknown one? No action registers or lists agent sessions.
options: Kernel registers a session
a session becomes known when Kernel first reads its working context
the owner types a session name
open_points.default_guess: Kernel registers a session with an action; the owner interface lists the known sessions.

open_points.subject: request a project switch
open_points.text: request a project switch ... unknown project refused
open_points.question: How does the agent name a target project when it never sees the catalogue, and does 'unknown project refused' disclose to the agent which projects exist? What happens when the target is archived?
options: free-text request the owner resolves
a project id, with existence hidden from the agent
a project id; unknown and archived ids are both refused
open_points.default_guess: The agent sends a project id or a free-text description; unknown and archived ids get the same answer as accepted ones, and the owner resolves the request.

open_points.subject: working context reference vs pinned project_id
open_points.text: an opaque reference to the project
open_points.question: R0-42 has a flow pin the `project_id` of its context, and the agent projection returns the id. Is the context's project reference the `project_id` or a separate opaque token?
options: the project_id itself
an opaque token, with project_id only in the projection
open_points.default_guess: The context carries the project_id; 'opaque' means the agent cannot derive anything else from it.

open_points.subject: import a project with its identity
open_points.text: the project under the identity it carries in its source, with its customer, object, rooms and pointers
open_points.question: Does an import keep the source's customer_ref, room ids and pointer ids and versions? R0-16 says a caller never supplies a customer_ref, and Registry mints room and pointer identities. What happens when an imported customer_ref collides with one production holds?
options: import keeps all ids, refusing conflicts
the project id is kept; customers, rooms and pointers are re-minted and mapped
open_points.default_guess: Every id is kept and any conflict is refused, as an explicit exception to R0-16 and R0-17 for import.

open_points.subject: create a project in test instances
open_points.text: the project with the identity Registry mints (R0-44)
open_points.question: R0-44 bounds minting to production. May a test instance still accept a caller-supplied project_id (R0-07), or does every instance mint?
options: every instance mints
test instances keep R0-07
open_points.default_guess: Every instance mints; caller ids enter only by import.

open_points.subject: retention expiry and end of relationship
open_points.text: A customer's contact data: until the relationship with the customer ends, plus one year.
open_points.question: Which action records that a relationship has ended, and who performs it? Which actor and action erase or anonymise data when a period ends, with what observable output and audit entry? The table has no row for either.
options: the owner marks a relationship ended; Registry erases on schedule
the end is derived from all of the customer's projects being archived
open_points.default_guess: The end is derived from the last project's archive; Registry runs a scheduled erasure that leaves an audit entry.

open_points.subject: R0-37 audit
open_points.text: Every significant operation leaves an audit entry
open_points.question: Which operations are significant? Are reads of personal data and refused requests included? This is not carried to a later state.
options: every change and every personal_data read
every change only
all operations, refusals included
open_points.default_guess: Every change, every personal_data read and every refused authorization.

open_points.subject: what Registry stores
open_points.text: Registry stores identity, the owner's choice of working project and pointers only.
open_points.question: The statement leaves out the customer contact data, object characteristics, switch requests and the audit log that Registry also stores. Should the statement name them?
options: extend the statement
treat them as part of 'identity'
open_points.default_guess: Extend the statement to list contact data, the object, switch requests and the audit log.

open_points.subject: standing of R0-45
open_points.text: the owner's answers of 2026-10-27 on its conflicts with that frame are recorded as R0-24 to R0-45
open_points.question: R0-45 is 'proposed to the owner ... no objection', not an owner answer. Does silence count as an owner decision under R0-15, or is R0-45 pending until the owner accepts it?
options: treat as accepted
list as open until confirmed
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as pending confirmation within the final acceptance of the whole.
